name: frontend-skills
description: React/TypeScript frontend + Go backend enforcement harness. 91 wired hooks across 100 scripts enforce patterns on every edit. Green != done: `test-warning-check` surfaces warnings on passing test/lint/type runs (DeprecationWarning, React `act()`, unhandled rejection, `@ts-ignore`); `ci-warning-audit` Stop-hook scans `gh run view --log` on green CI for deprecations / console warnings / skipped tests. 51 skills from TDD through CI-green PR, including /steelman anti-sycophancy guard + /snyk-ux-security per-path vuln sweep (JS + Go ecosystems; exploitability-triage first gate via `bun why`/`go mod why`/`govulncheck`; top-level direct dep bump first, parent dep bump second, resolutions/overrides/replace as last resort only with follow-up TODO to remove; React 18 pin + changelog-walked major bumps + no-deferral escalation; Go `snyk test --file=go.mod` + `go get -u` + `go mod tidy` + `govulncheck` verify). Session exit blocked while PR review threads remain unresolved. TypeScript escape hatches blocked at Edit. tsconfig strictness weakening blocked. Worktree isolation + branch safety hook-enforced. bun.lock + yarn.lock parity enforced (Snyk IO doesn't parse bun.lock). 21 LLM failure modes enforced: 7 Karpathy single-agent + 14 MAST multi-agent (Cemri et al. NeurIPS 2025). OWASP + STRIDE subset + snyk/bun audit. Core Web Vitals perf gate. MCP ban with CLI redirect (~20x token savings). Agent-browser wrap (~91% token reduction for AI browsing). 3-hat plan review (product/engineering/design). 9 agents (adds plan hats + karpathy reference), 5 routines. Opus 4.7 tuned, POSIX-friendly.

x-changelog.4.9.0: 2026-04-23 -- Green != done warnings gate. Two new hooks (89 -> 91 wired, 98 -> 100 scripts). (1) `test-warning-check.sh` (PostToolUse Bash): on exit=0 from `vitest` / `bun test` / `playwright` / `tsgo` / `tsc` / `biome` / `lint`, scans stdout + stderr for curated warning patterns -- Node `DeprecationWarning`, `ExperimentalWarning`, `(node:...) XxxWarning`, React `Warning: An update to .* inside a test was not wrapped in act`, `Warning: Each child in a list should have a unique "key"`, `Warning: validateDOMNesting`, `Warning: Failed prop type`, `Warning: Cannot update a component .* while rendering`, `Warning: Received .* for a non-boolean attribute`, `MaxListenersExceededWarning` / `PossibleEventEmitterMemoryLeak`, `UnhandledPromiseRejection` / `Unhandled Rejection` / `Unhandled Errors`, vitest `stderr |` during test, `Tests skipped N`, `@ts-expect-error`, `@ts-ignore`, `npm WARN deprecated`. Emits systemMessage nudge with file:line sample. Per-test-file escape `// allow: test-warning`; env `TEST_WARNINGS_ALLOW=1` globally. 3x same-kind streak escalates via warning-streak tracker. (2) `ci-warning-audit.sh` (Stop hook): gated on feature branch + session touched code + PR exists + all CI checks SUCCESS (pending/failing defers to lifecycle-stop). Resolves PR head SHA, fetches `gh run view <id> --log` with 45s timeout, pipes through grep on the same curated pattern, heads 30. Per-SHA cache in session dir so repeat Stops don't re-fetch the same log. `hook_warn` (non-blocking) with file:line sample + suggested full-log command. Disable via `CI_WARNING_AUDIT=0`. (3) CLAUDE.md Tests section + tdd/SKILL.md `When Done` checklist updated: zero warnings in local output AND CI, with escape hatch documented. Why: passing tests can silently spew deprecations, log errors, leak unhandled rejections -- noise that rots into real bugs when the lib actually removes the API. 'Green' was never the bar; zero warnings is.
x-changelog.4.8.0: 2026-04-22 -- /steelman anti-sycophancy skill (opt-in only). New skill at steelman/SKILL.md argues strongest opposite case with repo evidence on user assertions -- factual/causal/architectural claim types only (preference/goal/scope declined). Procedure: identify claim -> fan-out evidence gather (grep, read, run) -> write counter-argument with file:line refs -> verdict (confirmed | contradicted | mixed). User-invoked via `/steelman` slash only. **No ambient CLAUDE.md rule, no automatic hook fire, no telemetry log script** -- plugin consumers see zero behavior change unless they type `/steelman`. Ambient premise-check directive + jsonl telemetry were considered and held back pending real-world feedback on the opt-in surface; re-evaluate once /steelman fire-rate data exists from dogfooding. Why: LLM sycophancy risk when the user asserts something wrong and the model agrees by default -- /steelman forces the strongest counter-case with repo evidence before proceeding. Skills 47 -> 48 (registers the skill file that was previously on disk but unlisted).
x-changelog.4.7.0: 2026-04-22 -- /snyk-ux-security: exploitability-triage first-gate + top-level-first upgrade ladder + Go ecosystem parity. (1) Exploitability triage (new first gate): per finding decide REACHABLE vs NOT-REACHABLE before any bump. Inputs: advisory attack vector, `bun why <pkg>` / `go mod why <mod>`, direct-import grep, usage check vs vulnerable symbol. NOT-REACHABLE -> dismiss via `snyk ignore --id=<id> --reason='<specific why>' --expiry=<ISO date>` and document in PR under `Dismissed (not exploitable)` with CVE + symbol + reason + expiry. Expiry forces re-triage so dismissals do not rot (SLA audit trail). Reachable or credible vector -> proceed. (2) Upgrade priority ladder: 1. Direct dep bump (the package already in our manifest) -- default path. 2. Parent dep bump (the direct dep pulling the vuln transitive) -- second choice. 3. `resolutions` / `overrides` / `replace` only as last resort -- they do not scale, bloat lockfiles, force more overrides next week; each override gets a follow-up TODO to remove once upstream ships a fix, logged in a dedicated `Overrides added` PR section with blocker explanation. Why: node_modules bloat from reflex-adding resolutions when the CVE was never reachable; top-level bumps are upstream-tracked and self-maintaining. (3) Go ecosystem parity (new track alongside JS track): ecosystem detect per path -- `package.json` -> JS, `go.mod` -> Go, both present -> both tracks in same worktree, separate commits, single PR. Scan: `snyk test --file=go.mod` + `snyk monitor --file=go.mod` + `govulncheck -json ./...` (native call-graph reachability verdicts from the Go security team -- prefer its reachability verdict over raw CVE lists). Triage: non-reachable transitives dismissed with reason `govulncheck: not reachable from call graph`. Bump: `go get -u <mod>@<ver>` first, then parent, then `replace` directive last resort (with tracking issue). Sync: `go mod tidy` -- `go.mod` + `go.sum` commit together, never hand-edit. Verify: `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `govulncheck ./...` clean for addressed CVEs. PR gets `lang/go` label + backend team inferred from CODEOWNERS (`services/*`, `cmd/*`, paths with `go.mod`). Rule: do NOT bump `go 1.XX` toolchain directive as part of a CVE sweep -- separate change. (4) Docs: SKILL.md rewritten to 75 lines (110-line cap) with triage + ladder + Go track sections; REFERENCE.md gains `Exploitability triage`, `Upgrade priority`, `Go ecosystem notes` sections + expanded PR body template with `Dismissed` + `Overrides added` tables + per-ecosystem verify checklists. (5) Preserved: bun-only JS runtime; React 18 pin + `react19-blocked` skip; dual-lockfile invariant + lockfile-sync-check.sh drift guard; never-defer rule for real reachable vulns; sequential per-path worktree isolation. (6) Evals: +23 checks covering triage, ladder, and Go track (go.mod, govulncheck, go get -u, go mod tidy, go build/test/vet, snyk test --file=go.mod, replace directive last-resort, go.sum, call-graph reachability). Full suite 1819/1819 pass, zero skips.
